title: The valley of greed
hookLine: if a person had a valley of gold he'd want two (Bukhari)

cards: A valley full of gold. Not a bag of it, not a vault. A whole valley, ridge to ridge, glittering in the sun.
Surely that's the end of wanting. Surely a person standing on that ridge says: done. A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari answers in one plain sentence.
If the son of Adam had a valley of gold, he would want a second one. The valley doesn't fill the want. It teaches the want to count.

teach.h: A WANT THAT GROWS WITH HAVING.
teach.b: First, the shape of greed in this hadith. It isn't hunger for one thing; it's a want that grows with the having. Thirst closes when it's met: you drink, it's over.
Greed, as the hadith draws it, opens wider when you feed it.
Second, the line that follows: nothing fills the mouth of the son of Adam except dust. The dust of the grave. Only the end of a life ends that wanting.
But the hadith doesn't stop on dust: and Allah turns to whoever turns to him. The sentence ends on a door, not a grave.

Third, the Qur'an says it in two short lines, in Pickthall's words: "Rivalry in worldly increase distracteth you Until ye come to the graves." Rivalry, increase, graves: the same race, stopping only at the end.

And fourth, the cure, which the hadith doesn't put in poverty. The valley isn't the disease; the wanting is. Another hadith in al-Bukhari moves the riches somewhere else: richness isn't having many things.
Richness is richness of the soul. So enough isn't a number in a bank account. It's a place in the heart where the wanting can sit down.

how: Muslim teachers use the hadith of the valley of gold and the teaching that true richness is richness of the soul to warn against greed; contentment, called qana'ah, and gratitude are practiced as its cure.

games.q: what does “the valley of greed” mean?
o: the hunger of the poor for daily bread
a real valley of gold promised in paradise
a want that grows bigger the more it gets

p: fills the mouth of the son of Adam
until ye come to the graves

s: the hadith ends on dust filling the mouth, and nothing more
it goes on: Allah turns to whoever turns to him.

the disease is a want that grows with having; the cure is a rich soul, not poverty.

games.q: you're standing on the ridge above a valley of gold, all yours. by the hadith, what happens next?
games.why: the hadith says he'd want two. only dust fills that mouth, and yet Allah turns to whoever turns to him.

practice: Start with the breath: it came, and it was enough for this moment; then the seat under you, the last thing you ate, the roof overhead, one person who'd pick up if you called. Name each one quietly, and after each, the word: enough.
When the mind reaches for the next thing on the list, notice the reach and come back; if you pray, you can thank Allah for one of them by name.

wordCard.voice: The valley of greed. The hadith's picture of a want that grows with having: a valley of gold, and a wish for a second. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: richness of the soul, the hadith's name for true wealth.

carryVoice: Your line: enough is enough. Richness is richness of the soul. See you tomorrow, for the harm of backbiting.
